label: The hub's restraint enforcement is qualitative end to end: no LOC, line-budget, complexity or function-length mechanism exists in sk-code-quality or the shared universal standards, only the ladder's YAGNI rung and the P0/P1/P2 gate rule, while Ponytail carries a size metric, a correctness gate and behavior probes over the same concern. The gap is measurement, not gating. Classification: NEW.

Ponytail quantifies its test reflex as a rate (98% of risky logic ships with a test vs 68% without the skill) while the hub states the same reflex as a rule plus a scenario, so no trend is reportable; this is the measurable form of the test-reflex gap iteration 1 identified. Classification: NEW.

The quality mode's advisory envelope already carries per-severity dispositions and accepted deferrals, so a measurement-only size or test-rate signal has a recording slot that does not touch the gate contract and stays consistent with the prior LOC-as-gate rejection. Classification: NEW (small).

Comment hygiene in the hub is enforced by three independent gates (write-time warning, pre-commit block, CI block) with an escalation rule when the layers disagree on a blocking result, which is stronger than Ponytail's rule text plus behavior probe. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (stronger).

The advisory evidence-handoff envelope fixes its status to advisory and forbids pass, success or done, and may never replace the verification handoff, so the hub is stricter about self-verdict vocabulary than Ponytail's Verdict and scoreboard lines; Ponytail's complementary contribution in this area is its coverage disclosure, not its verdict line. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (stronger).

Author-side versus review-side separation is explicit and backed by tool authority in the hub (quality mode has no Write or Task authority and may not make passing claims; review mode forbids Edit), where Ponytail separates the roles by instruction text only. Classification: ALREADY-ADOPTED (structural).

The quality mode's machine-readable router independently acknowledges that the deterministic skill-benchmark router-replay it was written for has since been retired, confirming from a second site that the removed measurement path is a known, documented gap whose corpus and replay design remain in place. Classification: NEW (small; corroborates iteration 5's LOST finding).
